suggestion.title: AitM Phishing Link Click from Office 365
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Microsoft 365 AitM phishing attacks. Pipeline missed detection for phishing link engagement, which is the initial access trigger for credential capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Sign-In Risk events or Impossible Travel alerts in AAD logs correlating with click timestamps from email security gateways. Look for sign-in events immediately following phishing link clicks from URLs not in organization's whitelist.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via AitM Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions AitM capturing credentials. Pipeline did not detect forced re-authentication or proxy interception patterns typical of these attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sign-ins preceded by credential reset alerts or from high-risk IP reputation services. Look for sign-in methods inconsistent with user baseline (e.g., browser popup re-auth flows from unexpected geos).

suggestion.title: Abnormal Email Collection from Compromised Finance Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers hijacked accounts to collect payroll and finance emails. Pipeline failed to surface detections for mass mailbox access or export activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual search patterns in Exchange targeting payroll keywords (salary, W-2, direct deposit). Detect bulk mail access to finance-group mailboxes from newly compromised accounts or IP addresses without prior access history.

suggestion.title: Valid Cloud Account Abuse Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: AitM results in account takeover using stolen credentials. Pipeline did not generate UC for compromised account activity diverging from user baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish user activity baseline (login times, geos, device types). Alert on sign-ins from new countries within 1 hour of phishing campaign spike, or mailbox access outside historical 95th percentile hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Forwarding Rule Creation on Finance Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attackers often persist access via forwarding rules to exfiltrate future payroll/finance emails. Pipeline omitted this common persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbox rule creation or forwarding updates on accounts flagged as compromised in finance/HR groups. Alert if rule targets external domains or cloud storage services.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel: Sign-In Geo Spike + Email Access
suggestion.rationale: AitM attacks from attacker infrastructure create impossible travel patterns (user in New York office, then 'sign-in' from Russia minutes later). Pipeline ignored travel anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate sign-in location with user's Office 365 mailbox access geo. Flag sign-ins from countries not in user's historical access pattern that precede finance mailbox queries.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Smuggling via Content-Length Desynchronization
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'novel HTTP Desync Techniques' as the primary attack vector. Pipeline missed this foundational detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with conflicting or ambiguous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers sent to vulnerable web servers (e.g., Apache). Flag requests where Content-Length and chunked encoding coexist, or where whitespace/case variations in Transfer-Encoding appear. Group by target server version to correlate with known vulnerable Apache releases.

suggestion.title: Apache Server Exploitation via HTTP Protocol Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Apache Zero-Day'. Pipeline should have surfaced exploitation attempts against Apache HTTP Server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Apache access and error logs for malformed HTTP requests, unusual header combinations, or POST requests with ambiguous message boundaries. Correlate with Apache version information to identify which versions are targeted. Alert on requests that result in HTTP 400/500 errors followed by successful connection reuse.

suggestion.title: Malformed HTTP Headers and Boundary Manipulation Attacks
suggestion.rationale: HTTP desynchronization exploits rely on crafted headers and request boundaries. Article describes this as a key technique but pipeline generated no detection content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests with non-standard header formatting: tabs or spaces before header names, duplicate Content-Length headers with different values, Transfer-Encoding headers with invalid parameters or extra whitespace. Establish baseline of normal Content-Length distributions per endpoint and alert on statistical outliers.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Activity Following HTTP Desync Attack Success
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates this enables a zero-day; successful exploitation would be followed by attacker post-exploitation. Pipeline failed to model the complete attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful HTTP desync exploitation, monitor for unusual process spawning from Apache worker processes, outbound network connections from Apache, or abnormal file modifications in web root directories. Desync attacks that achieve RCE will show POST request patterns followed by command execution within seconds.

suggestion.title: Connection Reuse and Response Interception via HTTP Desync
suggestion.rationale: HTTP desync fundamentally exploits connection pooling and response interception. Article highlights this novel technique; pipeline did not map it to detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns where a single TCP connection carries multiple HTTP requests with misaligned request/response boundaries. Alert on frontend/backend disagreement on message boundaries (frontend sees benign request, backend sees attacker payload). Monitor for requests sent to backend before receiving complete response from prior request.

suggestion.title: NAT Table Manipulation & Rogue ARP Entries
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'manipulating NAT tables'—this is the core attack mechanism. Pipeline extracted zero detection logic for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ARP replies from unexpected sources or broadcast-to-unicast ARP mapping changes. Detect sudden creation of static NAT entries on edge routers or gateways, especially bidirectional mappings for IPs not previously seen. Flag ARP gratuitous replies and mismatches between Layer 2 and Layer 3 forwarding tables.

suggestion.title: TCP Session Hijacking via Sequence Prediction
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'hijack TCP sessions'—fundamental attack step with zero detection coverage proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TCP packets with sequence numbers that fall within an active session's window but originate from unexpected source IPs. Flag sudden MTU/window size changes mid-stream, duplicate ACKs with payload, or RST/FIN packets from third-party IPs targeting established connections.

suggestion.title: DNS Response Spoofing from Unauthorized Resolvers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'spoof DNS'—attack outcome clearly stated, no detection hypothesis generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when DNS responses arrive from IPs not in the organization's authoritative resolver list. Detect response latencies or TTLs inconsistent with expected nameserver behavior. Flag DNS responses to queries that were never sent from monitored clients (unsolicited replies).

suggestion.title: Persistent ARP Cache Poisoning via NAT State Injection
suggestion.rationale: NAT manipulation combined with session hijacking implies sustained cache poisoning; pipeline has no persistence-phase detection.
log_sources: Windows Event 4625 (auth failures from poisoned IPs)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated ARP entries with identical MAC but rotating IP addresses, or static ARP bindings that persist across DHCP lease cycles. Correlate failed authentication attempts from spoofed IPs with ARP anomalies in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Path Packet Injection (TCP Data Stream Corruption)
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking TCP sessions typically involves injecting packets from attacker IP; no detection for mid-stream injection or checksum anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TCP packets with valid checksum and sequence numbers but originating from IPs not previously seen in that connection's handshake. Flag application-level protocol violations (HTTP request without proper SYN from that source, FTP commands from non-initiator IP) within established flows.

suggestion.title: Gateway/Router Configuration Changes Enabling NAT Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting or modifying NAT requires access to routing infrastructure—no detection for unauthorized config changes or privilege escalation on network devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful SSH/Telnet login to routers/firewalls from non-standard management IPs. Monitor for configuration backups or syslog exports to suspicious destinations. Flag changes to NAT tables, static routes, or ACLs that deviate from change-management schedules.

suggestion.title: GitHub Issue Interaction from Anomalous CLI Tool Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states GitHub Issue feature is the delivery mechanism: 'GitHub Issue Reach CI Workflow Secrets.' Suggests attackers create or interact with issues via Claude Code or Gemini CLI tools in ways that bypass normal issue-filing workflows or enable secret exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub API calls originating from Claude Code or Gemini CLI processes, especially creating issues or posting comments that reference environment variables, secrets, or CI tokens. Alert on issue creation followed immediately by secret access patterns.

suggestion.title: CI Workflow Secret Access Following GitHub Issue Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates the attack reaches 'CI Workflow Secrets' via the GitHub Issue vector. This implies a second stage where issue creation or manipulation triggers secret exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect accesses to CI workflow environment variables or stored secrets within seconds/minutes of unusual GitHub issue activity. Look for secrets being logged, exported, or transmitted outside the CI environment.

suggestion.title: Claude Code / Gemini CLI Executing Unauthorized Git Operations
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability names the tools explicitly; the flaw likely allows these tools to perform git/GitHub operations (issue creation, push, cloning) without proper authentication boundaries or user consent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Claude Code or Gemini CLI spawning unexpected git, curl, or python subprocess calls that interact with GitHub API endpoints. Flag tool execution with GitHub CLI flags or API tokens being passed as arguments or via environment variables.

suggestion.title: Secret Exfiltration Through CI Workflow Logs or Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: CI secrets compromised in workflows often leak through logs, build outputs, or error messages. Article's severity (crit) implies secrets actually reached attacker, not just vulnerable to reach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search CI logs for environment variable references, token patterns (Bearer, ghp_, aws_), or secret-like strings being printed, uploaded to external URLs, or committed. Correlate with Claude Code / Gemini CLI process timelines.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised CI Secrets to Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: CI workflow secrets typically include cloud provider credentials (AWS, Azure, GCP). Once extracted via the GitHub-issue vector, attacker gains lateral movement to production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unusual API calls in cloud provider logs (AWS assume-role, Azure token refresh, GCP service-account usage) with timestamps of CI secret compromise. Flag API patterns inconsistent with normal CI/CD automation.

suggestion.title: Developer Tool Injection / Supply-Chain Trust Abuse (Claude Code / Gemini CLI)
suggestion.rationale: The flaw in Claude Code and Gemini CLI themselves represents a supply-chain attack vector—trusted developer tools become attack conduits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected network connections from Claude Code or Gemini CLI binaries to unusual C2 infrastructure or credential-harvesting servers. Track version updates and behavioral changes in these tools.

suggestion.title: Redis Brute-Force / Credential Spray Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-year Redis attack campaign; no defense detection around high-volume failed auth or unusual port 6379 connection attempts. 'Redis Attacks Dating Back To 2020' implies repeated exploitation waves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for >50 failed AUTH commands to Redis port 6379 from single source IP within 5min window, or connection attempts from IPs with no historical Redis interaction. Redis slowlog and netflow data should flag non-standard query patterns or data exfiltration volume anomalies.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Artifact Integrity Violations
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Supply Chain Campaign' but pipeline produced no detection for compromised package artifacts, malicious dependencies, or repository manipulation. This is a primary attack vector for TeamPCP's campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden code-signing certificate changes, unsigned package uploads to internal/public repos, or version-rollback anomalies. Correlate with unusual build-server process execution (cargo, npm, pip install from external/untrusted sources).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Redis Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Redis exploitation often enables command execution; article describes attacks 'dating back to 2020' without detection for EVAL, Lua-script injection, or ACL bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect EVAL/EVALSHA commands with embedded OS shell syntax (bash/cmd separators), child processes spawned by redis-server process, or unexpected sockets opened by Redis service. Cross-reference with file-write events to /tmp or scheduled-task creation.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Compromised Redis Instances
suggestion.rationale: Multi-year campaign implies persistent C2; no detection for data exfiltration channels, DGA resolution patterns, or out-of-band command channels established through Redis pub/sub or keyspace notifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Redis instances establishing connections to non-whitelisted external IPs on high ports; detect DNS queries for short-lived or single-use domains from server IPs; correlate data exfil volume spikes (>1GB/hour) from Redis host to external CIDR ranges.

suggestion.title: Exposed Redis Instance Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: 'Redis Attacks' campaigns typically begin with scanning public-facing instances; article provides no baseline for detecting unusual INFO, CONFIG, or KEYS commands that indicate reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on first-time INFO, COMMAND, CONFIG GET, or KEYS * commands from external IPs; establish baseline of legitimate administrative commands and flag deviations. Monitor for tool-like patterns (sequential enumeration of all keys, rapid DB selection).

suggestion.title: TeamPCP Malware Staging via Package Repository
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain vector implies payload delivery through legitimate channels; no detection for unusual package publish patterns, version anomalies, or malware-signature matches on artifacts attributed to TeamPCP campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories (npm, PyPI, cargo, nuget) for new publisher accounts or packages with filenames/descriptions referencing Redis, database, or infrastructure keywords. Flag rapid version-bumps with large binary diffs; cross-ref against YARA rules for TeamPCP payloads.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation Triggers GitHub Actions Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states worm is 'extracting GitHub Actions runner secrets'—core attack vector. Pipeline must detect when npm postinstall code accesses GitHub environment variables or token stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned during npm install that read GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_ACTIONS, or secrets.* environment variables, followed by outbound network connection. Look for node/npm processes accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.git-credentials, or GitHub config directories.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Establishes Ethereum Smart Contract Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing'—detection must capture blockchain-based command infrastructure. This deviates from typical C2 and evades traditional network signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS to known Ethereum RPC endpoints (infura.io, alchemy.com, ankr.com) or direct contract calls to unfamiliar smart contract addresses from npm/node processes. Flag transaction payloads containing exfiltrated data or configuration bytes.

suggestion.title: Rapid Self-Propagating npm Package Version Updates and Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline describes 'self-propagating npm worm'—must detect when infected package rapidly injects itself or malicious dependencies into downstream packages to spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish operations and npm registry API calls for anomalous patterns: multiple version bumps within minutes, unexpected dependency additions, or modified package.json pointing to attacker-controlled registries. Cross-correlate with stolen npm tokens.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Secrets Encoded in Blockchain Transactions
suggestion.rationale: Article combines 'extracting GitHub Actions secrets' with 'Ethereum smart contracts for C2'—exfiltration method likely encodes stolen credentials into transaction data to bypass DLP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub Actions secret access (via process monitoring of environment variable reads) with subsequent Ethereum transaction creation. Decode transaction input data to identify embedded Base64/hex-encoded secrets. Flag low-value transactions with oversized data payloads.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Malicious npm Package Install with Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'npm worm'—initial access vector is compromised package installation triggering arbitrary code execution in postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install or npm update spawns unexpected child processes (especially shells, curl, wget, or network tools) within postinstall script context. Flag packages with suspicious dependencies or unusual postinstall script size/obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Vishing campaign targeting MFA/passkey enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'helpdesk vishing' campaigns where operators 'contact employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings.' No detection logic for this social-engineering vector was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound calls from numbers spoofing corporate helpdesk to employee personal phones referencing MFA/passkey enrollment during off-hours or in geographic anomaly. Correlation with subsequent phishing emails in the same timeframe increases confidence.

suggestion.title: MITM phishing kit delivery via domain impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Victims are then directed to domains impersonating the targeted employee's company that host adversary-in-the-middle phishing kits designed to steal credentials and session cookies in real time.' No detection for credential interception or domain spoofing was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lookalike domains registered with FQDN impersonation patterns hosting phishing/MITM kits. Monitor SSO logs for unusual user agents, impossible-travel logins followed by credential re-entry, or MFA prompts immediately re-authenticated without expected friction.

suggestion.title: SSO dashboard access with rapid multi-cloud service enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'After stealing Microsoft 365 or Okta single-sign-on accounts, the attackers log into the SSO dashboard, which gives access to all the cloud platforms that are linked to the account.' This lateral movement and cloud resource discovery pattern is critical but was not mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSO dashboard access from new IP/geography immediately after account compromise. Detect rapid enumeration of linked SaaS applications (AWS, Azure, GCP, Salesforce, etc.) within 10-60 minutes of SSO login. Correlate with behavioral anomalies.

suggestion.title: Mass cloud storage exfiltration post-SSO compromise
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed the exfiltration phase: 'the hackers then use automated tools to steal data from all cloud services they gain access to.' Large-scale data extraction from compromised cloud accounts is the tactical impact requiring immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect volumetric data downloads from cloud storage (SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive) to external accounts/IPs within hours of SSO compromise. Flag >100GB transfers in 24h when user baseline is <1GB. Monitor for export-to-personal-email or mass download patterns.

suggestion.title: Security alert and notification suppression from compromised mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'delete security notifications and password-reset emails from compromised inboxes.' This defense-evasion tactic to hide breach traces was entirely absent from generated detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mass deletion of security-related emails (MFA changes, suspicious login alerts, password-reset notices) from high-value user mailboxes. Detect bulk email deletion rules targeting senders like 'security@', 'noreply@alerts'. Correlate timing with SSO compromise.

suggestion.title: Post-exfiltration extortion demand communication
suggestion.rationale: Article notes ransom payments: 'Between January and May 2026, GTIG tracked over $10.6 million USD in Bitcoin payments to group wallets. While initial demands reach upwards of $3 million, operators routinely settle for around $750,000 USD.' Extortion messaging and ransom negotiation should trigger defined incident workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound emails from known UNC6671/BlackFile/Falcon/Redact/Pink/Helix extortion infrastructure or Tor-hosted leak sites announcing data theft with specific dataset references matching internal classifications. Alert immediately on receipt.

suggestion.title: Passkey Extraction or Cloning Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Pass the Passkey' and description 'passkey implementation gaps' indicate passkey theft/transfer is the attack vector. No detection rule was generated despite this being the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious processes accessing passkey storage locations (e.g., Chrome sync, authenticator databases, key material exports). Flag unusual file I/O or registry access by non-browser processes targeting credential storage. Look for exports of CBOR-encoded passkey structures or private key material.

suggestion.title: User Verified Flag Bypass in Authentication Events
suggestion.rationale: Description explicitly states 'relying parties fail to validate the User Verified flag, reducing MFA to a single factor.' Pipeline generated no detection for this validation-gap attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for passkey assertions missing User Verified indicator. Correlate successful logins via passkey without biometric/PIN confirmation. Flag sessions where MFA evidence is incomplete or timestamps indicate passkey was used offline.

suggestion.title: MFA Downgrade via Passkey-Only Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacks reducing 'MFA to a single factor' by bypassing secondary authentication. No use case covered credential-only MFA bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify authentication successes where passkey is accepted but secondary MFA factors (TOTP, push approval, U2F confirmation) are missing or skipped. Correlate with rapid authentication success times inconsistent with user verification workflows.

suggestion.title: Google Authenticator Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'google authenticator' and 'malware'. Pipeline should flag indicators of TOTP/passkey extraction from Google Authenticator storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes reading Google Authenticator's encrypted database files, attempting to hook cryptographic functions, or accessing the app's shared preferences. Flag suspicious memory reads or screen capture events when Authenticator is active.

suggestion.title: Passkey Sync Anomalies Across Trusted Devices
suggestion.rationale: Stolen passkeys are typically synced across attacker-controlled devices. Article implies device-level compromise or credential cloning. No detection for unauthorized sync patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on passkey sync events from new or geographically anomalous devices. Correlate with successful authentications from those devices within 24 hours of sync. Flag rapid sequential registrations of new trusted devices in passkey provider (Google, Apple, Dashlane, etc.).

suggestion.title: Authentication via Cloned Passkey Without User Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: using stolen passkey to authenticate as victim without completing verification steps. Pipeline missed detection for out-of-band passkey replay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful WebAuthn/CTAP assertions from unfamiliar authenticators or lacking expected user verification proof. Correlate passkey authentication success with absence of corresponding browser push notifications or FIDO device interaction logs. Flag logins from IP ranges inconsistent with user's historical access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-63077' is in CISA KEV with active exploitation. Pipeline generated zero hunts despite template reference to asset-exposure pattern. Substitute into standard scanner query.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for TeamCity instances running vulnerable versions. Flag any instances exposed to internet-facing assets. Correlate with patch due date (2026-08-08) to identify remediation gaps.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution' but pipeline captured no execution-phase detections. This is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to TeamCity agent endpoints that succeed (200/302 responses). Flag POST requests to agent polling endpoints without valid authentication tokens. Correlate with process execution from TeamCity service account.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'agent polling protocol' as specific exploit vector. Pipeline completely omitted protocol-level detection despite this being the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed or oversized payloads in TeamCity agent polling protocol traffic. Monitor for serialized Java object patterns in agent requests. Flag rapid polling attempts from single source IP. Correlate with known deserialization gadget signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE from TeamCity Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows RCE but pipeline generated zero post-compromise detections for command execution following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from TeamCity service account (typically `teamcity` user). Flag execution of shell interpreters, reconnaissance tools, or file transfer utilities. Correlate with successful agent polling requests in preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Deserialization Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'deserialization of untrusted data' but pipeline produced no detection for deserialization attack patterns or Java exception spikes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity logs for Java deserialization exceptions, ClassNotFoundException spikes, or stream corruption errors. Track gadget chain library presence (commons-collections, ysoserial indicators). Flag successful RCE attempts followed by exception clearing or log deletion.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: KEV entry does not restrict impact to RCE on TeamCity host. Post-compromise lateral movement is standard after agent compromise. Pipeline omitted this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from TeamCity host to other infrastructure post-exploitation (ports 22, 445, 3389). Flag credential theft indicators from TeamCity config stores or build logs. Detect agent re-provisioning to additional hosts via agent polling.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Exposed Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable via unauthenticated access to agent polling protocol; asset exposure is the first control gate and template explicitly references asset-exposure hunts as canonical for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Internet-exposed TeamCity instances on default ports (8111 for UI, polling endpoint) via port scans, successful HTTP connections from external IPs, or HTTPS certificate scanning. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results showing unpatched TeamCity versions.

suggestion.title: Agent Polling Protocol Deserialization Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability...via the agent polling protocol' as attack vector; this is the exploitation phase and should trigger detection on payload submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious serialized Java object payloads or malformed deserialization requests sent to TeamCity agent polling endpoints. Look for base64-encoded payloads with Java serialization magic bytes (0xACED) or gadget-chain indicators in POST requests to /agent paths.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Service RCE Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote code execution'; successful exploitation will spawn child processes from the TeamCity service account (typically teamcity or java process); post-exploitation detection is essential given CISA KEV active-exploitation context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from TeamCity Java process (java.exe, catalina process) especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or reverse-shell payloads. Baseline TeamCity service process trees and alert on deviations including network egress from spawned children.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article notes agent polling protocol as attack vector; compromised TeamCity agents frequently enable lateral movement to connected build nodes or infrastructure services; missing hunt for inter-agent communication abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous network connections from TeamCity agents to internal infrastructure (build nodes, artifact repositories, VCS servers) that deviate from baseline polling patterns. Flag agent-to-agent or agent-to-infrastructure communication during off-hours or with unexpected protocols/ports.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Credential Harvesting from Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, TeamCity's build logs and artifact repositories commonly contain hardcoded credentials, API keys, and deployment secrets; article's RCE capability makes this a high-value collection point typically not modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity artifact directories, build logs, and config files for unexpected file reads or exfiltration attempts post-compromise. Alert on grep/find operations targeting credential patterns (AWS_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, password=) from the TeamCity service context.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated Agent Polling Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote code execution via the agent polling protocol' — pipeline generated no detection for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity instances for suspicious HTTP/HTTPS requests to agent polling endpoints from external or untrusted sources. Flag any agent registration or polling requests lacking valid authentication tokens or coming from non-agent IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in TeamCity Agent Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability mechanism — requires detection of malicious serialized objects in agent communication streams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious Java serialization patterns (magic bytes 0xACED0005 or Java serialized object headers) in TeamCity agent-to-server communications, particularly combined with unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) from the TeamCity Java process.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-63077 Exploitation Attempt via Agent Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-63077 but pipeline returned empty IOCs; need specific detection rule keyed to this CVE identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal TeamCity agent polling behavior (frequency, payload size, source IPs). Alert on sudden deviations: oversized payloads in agent protocol, agent polling from external IPs, or malformed protocol messages that might indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from TeamCity Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE outcome but pipeline missed detection for the execution phase; deserialization typically leads to arbitrary command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity Java processes (typically restricted to agent or internal utilities). Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or suspicious executable invocations with TeamCity service account as parent.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Version Enumeration and Pre-Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article targets unpatched TeamCity installations; attackers must identify vulnerable versions during reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to TeamCity version-disclosure endpoints (/buildServer/version.xml, /buildServer/, /login page version strings, or server headers). Alert on multiple requests to these endpoints from single external IP, indicating active version probing.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Agent Polling Protocol Exploitation Attempt (CVE-2026-63077)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability...via the agent polling protocol'. This is the explicit attack vector; must detect malformed or weaponized payloads sent to agent communication channels from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network traffic to TeamCity agent endpoints (default port 9090, agent polling URLs) containing serialized Java objects, unusual protocol markers, or bytecode patterns. Baseline legitimate agent registration and polling; alert on unauthenticated or malformed requests from internet-facing sources.

suggestion.title: Exposed TeamCity Instance Asset Discovery (CVE-2026-63077)
suggestion.rationale: Article: active CISA KEV exploitation. Must identify vulnerable instances exposed to internet. CVE-2026-63077 with federal due date 2026-08-08 is the scanning IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan/identify TeamCity web interface (port 8111 typical) and agent communication ports reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-63077. Flag instances without patching confirmation by 2026-08-08.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated RCE Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote code execution'. Detect command spawning or process execution immediately following exploit-window network activity to agent polling endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious agent-protocol network activity with unexpected child processes spawned by TeamCity process or agent service accounts within 5–30 seconds. Flag shell commands, binary downloads, or reverse shells absent from baseline TeamCity operations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Agent Registration or Polling Frequency Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'agent polling protocol' as attack surface. Exploitation may involve rogue agent registration or abnormal polling cadence signaling active C2 or post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity agent registration logs for new agents from unexpected IPs/hostnames. Alert on agent polling frequencies deviating from baseline or occurring outside maintenance windows. Track failed registration attempts preceding RCE.

Flag malformed payloads, requests with serialization gadgets, or connection patterns inconsistent with baseline agent registration. suggestion.title: Suspicious Agent Registration Events in TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization vulnerability via agent polling protocol could enable attacker to register malicious agents. Legitimate agents register from known infrastructure; unexpected registrations from untrusted sources indicate exploitation attempt.
